qualification: The minimum requirement of 50% aggregate marks in Matriculation is not applicable to candidates belonging to SC/ST/PwBD categories. If a candidate wishes to modify or correct the online application after submission, a fee of ₹50/- is charged for each occasion; however, registration details cannot be modified.
selection_process: Selection is purely merit-based, with no written examination. The merit list for each unit is prepared using thepercentage of marks in Matriculation (minimum 50% aggregate) plus ITI marksin the relevant trade; the final panel is based on the average of the two. || For Medical Laboratory Technician (Pathology) and (Radiology), merit is based on Matriculation marks plus 12th Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology) marks. || Calculation uses marks obtained inall subjectsof Matriculation/12th, not select subjects, and the average ITI marks across all semesters (or the National Trade Certificate marks). || Merit lists are prepared unit-wise, trade-wise and community-wise, in descending order of percentage, equal to the number of notified slots. || Shortlisted candidates are called forDocument Verification (DV)to the extent of 1.5 times the notified vacancies. || A candidate is considered for only one combination of Unit-Department-Trade based on merit and order of preference; once selected against a higher preference, all lower preferences are automatically cancelled. || In case of a tie in marks, the older candidate (by age) is ranked higher; if date of birth is also the same, the candidate who passed Matriculation earlier is ranked higher.

qualification: (A) Essential: || Passed 12th (+2 stage) or its equivalent examination with not less than 50% marks in the aggregate for NTPC categories. Only candidates qualifying Stage-I are eligible for the Stage-II recruitment process. || Candidates to the extent of only 5 times the number of vacancies, in order of merit, who have scored a minimum of 40% marks out of 50 in the written examination, will be called for practical demonstration and marking of testimonials/prizes. The merit list of the written examination will be the criterion for shortlisting. || After clearing Stage-I and Stage-II, and on the recommendation of the Recruitment Committee, the candidate will be sent for medical examination at a Railway Hospital, as per order of merit. The duration of the Written Test is 60 minutes, with a qualifying percentage of 40%. || Assessment of talent will be in the relevant cultural discipline, based on Practical Demonstration and Testimonials/Prizes examination. || The time and venue of the written test, practical demonstration, and document verification will be fixed by the Railways and intimated to eligible candidates in due course. No request for postponement of the written test, practical demonstration, or document verification will be entertained under any circumstances. || Note: The written examination and proficiency test shall be held at Maligaon, Guwahati.
